content:
maria: Heads-up — enterprise customer (acct: acme-inc) reports streaming sessions that stop after 2–4 very small chunks. Client reconnects and sometimes receives duplicate tokens (billing spike). Happened behind ALB -> Cloudflare Worker -> origin. Request-id: r-9f7c2a.

jonathan: Oof. Any example of the raw chunk boundary? do we have capture or app logs? :eyes:

maria: Pasting trimmed trace from customer's SDK logs:
```
[2026-03-15T18:12:02Z] req=r-9f7c2a -> recv chunk: "data: \"Hi\"\n\n" (18 bytes)
[2026-03-15T18:12:09Z] recv chunk: "data: \" \"\n\n" (6 bytes)
[2026-03-15T18:12:20Z] connection closed by remote, sdk reconnecting -> new req=r-9f7c2b
```
They also attached an nginx access log from their edge that shows `200` then a `closed` at T+18s.

ben_sre: Two quick suspects: 1) intermediate buffering/coalescing that swallows very small trailing chunks, 2) idle-probe/timeout causing half-close while origin still streaming. ALB idle timeout is 60s by default but CF Worker or nginx might have shorter timeouts or WAF rules.

support-bot: Related alert: streaming-reconnects spike for acme-inc between 2026-03-15T18:10 and 18:20 (spike +23%).

maria: Customer topology: mobile SDK -> Cloudflare (sockets proxied) -> ALB -> NLB -> Envoy -> app. They say Cloudflare WAF was recently toggled to "Managed ruleset: medium".

jonathan: WAF could be aggregating or dropping tiny chunks (some WAFs normalize payloads). Also watch out for `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` with tiny 0-length chunks; some proxies expect CRLF framing and may buffer until larger chunk seen.

ben_sre: Repro plan (I can run): 1) curl direct to origin bypassing ALB/CF, 2) curl through ALB only, 3) curl through CF -> ALB, compare chunk boundaries and TCP FIN timing. Use `tcpdump -s 0 -w` to capture. Example curl cmd we use for streaming tests:
```
curl -v -N "https://$ENDPOINT/stream?prompt=test" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -H "X-Request-ID: r-test-1" \n  --http1.1
```
Use `-N` to disable buffering on curl client.

maria: Customer did a capture — attached pcap shows origin sent three small chunks then a FIN immediately after the third chunk. Cloudflare responded with a `FIN` earlier (race). They suspect WAF flagged small chunk pattern and closed connection.

jonathan: If origin FIN immediately follows the last chunk, some proxies may coalesce the last bytes into kernel buffers and not flush to client before closing. That can produce missing tiny chunks. Workarounds: ensure server sends a final `\n` or heartbeat chunk (`:\n\n`) periodically, or ensure `Connection: keep-alive` semantics are preserved and proxies configured to stream small writes immediately.

ben_sre: For nginx/ALB/Envoy checks: - nginx: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on;` and `proxy_set_header Connection "";` or set `X-Accel-Buffering: no`. - Envoy: ensure `flush_downstream_on_remote_reset` not swallowing chunks; check `stream_idle_timeout` and `downstream_connection_idle_timeout`. - ALB: confirm idle timeout isn't being lowered by customer's infra (should be >= 60s). - Cloudflare: check WAF rules and proxy buffering flags (Workers can buffer responses).

maria: Customer tried sending `:\n\n` heartbeats every 10s and saw much fewer reconnects; they haven't confirmed duplication/billing reduction yet.

support-bot: Billing note: duplicate token usage occurs when client reconnects and server replays same completion. Consider idempotency key or server-side session resume to avoid double-billing while we investigate.

jonathan: Can we add a short-term mitigation: 1) server emits `:keepalive\n\n` every 12s, 2) Cloudflare rule to disable buffering on that route, 3) ALB stickiness to keep same TCP path? Any config we can flip without infra change?

ben_sre: I can run an origin-to-edge bypass test and share diffs by EOD. Also will query CF for any recent WAF rule hits for r-9f7c2a. If WAF logged `request-body-inspection` matches, we can escalate.

maria: assigning to @ben_sre to run full repro and @jonathan to coordinate with Cloudflare contact. Customer wants ETA within 24h.

ben_sre: Action items:
- reproduce via curl + tcpdump (in progress)
- check Envoy/nginx flush settings and forward config diff
- request Cloudflare WAF audit logs for request-id r-9f7c2a
- propose short-term keepalive heartbeat and idempotency guidance to customer
ETA: 18 hours.

jonathan: I'll ping CF and get rule audit. I'll also add a quick KB snippet to support: `Streaming: proxy buffering & tiny-chunk issues` with the common fixes.

maria: Thanks — please post repro pcap and a minimal curl diff here when done. Customer is OK with temporary heartbeats. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Deploy reminder: please don't flip global CF buffering flags without regional rollback plan.

ben_sre: Will post results in this thread.

maria: Closing loop later — keep thread for postmortem notes.
